Reading Paragraphs From Screenshots

1 Introduction

Translating text that appears on a screen is harder than translating a document, because the text has already been laid out. Every line break was chosen by a typesetting engine and not by the author, so a sentence is often cut in the middle of a phrase.

A translator that treats each visual line as a separate unit will therefore produce a translation that reads badly, and it may even move words from one line to the next without anyone noticing (Smith et al., 2018). We recover whole paragraphs from the geometry of the recognized lines instead.

  • Headings are never merged with the text below them.
  • Every list item starts a new unit of its own.

Figure 1: Lines that belong to one paragraph are joined into a single block before translation.

2 Method

Two lines belong together when the upper line is full, its sentence is not finished, and the lower line is the natural continuation of it. A line that stops early, ends with a period or starts a new item is left alone, because merging it would be worse than not merging it at all.

Hyphenated words such as inter-national are joined without a space, so the translator sees the word the author wrote.
